newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rugby Union-Deans tips 1997 NPC as toughest so far.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-Deans tips 1997 NPC as toughest so far.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, July 30 - This year's National Provincial Championship (NPC) will be the toughest in the rugby competition's 21-year history, according to new Canterbury coach Robbie Deans.
Deans on Wednesday named Todd Blackadder as captain and Mark Mayerhofler as vice-captain for the first-division series, saying their attitude epitomised what he wanted to see from his side.
The rest of the squad will be named on Sunday night.
Canterbury's first game is at night, against Wellington, at Lancaster Park on August 18.
Deans said all eight games in the round-robin series would be difficult.
"Players are facing challenges not previously experienced. This year will be the toughest NPC competition of any gone before."
Deans said the age of professionalism would usher in an intensity to rugby not seen in the NPC before.
"We can't afford to be slow starters this year.
"We want to be the best attacking side in the competition, with or without the ball."
The former All Black fullback said the Canterbury players were being instilled with a culture of dedication to performance and the red and black jersey.
The aim of the side would be to fulfil the public's expectations.
Canterbury's NPC players are being rewarded for their performances with cash bonuses for appearances and wins.
A bigger bonus could be handed out at the end of the season, depending on if, or by how much, the union surpassed its budgeted revenue.
Canterbury are expected to be short of experienced locks, with likely starter Steve Lancaster leading the way with only four NPC games under his belt.
Deans said Blackadder, one of the country's leading blindside flankers would most likely play all his games on the side of the scrum, not at lock where he filled in for most of last NPC season.
Canterbury's second game this year is away against Southland, a team Deans said was shaping up like a World Invitation 15.
